passage: Pranav here. I work in the same design team as Ishita, so I have watched this for months. Our manager always hands the new client pitches to Meera and asks her opinion first in reviews. Ishita's mockups get "fine, ship it." Last Thursday she stayed until eight and put a one-page summary of her project results on the shared drive, time saved and revisions cut, then mentioned it in the team update. After that she asked the manager what the criteria were for leading a pitch. The manager said "let's talk about it" and looked at the clock. Ishita went back to her desk, her mouth a thin line. I don't know if she felt small or just tired, but over lunch she told me she is giving it until the year-end review before she decides about moving on.

qa.q: What did Ishita put on the shared drive?
qa.a: A one-page summary of her project results, showing time saved and revisions cut.

qa.q: What does the thin line of Ishita's mouth suggest?
qa.a: She may feel let down or overlooked after the vague reply, though Pranav cannot be certain.

qa.q: What could Ishita do before the year-end review?
qa.a: Keep making her results visible and ask again, in writing, for clear criteria.

qa.q: How might the manager have seen the question about criteria?
qa.a: The manager may have been caught off guard, since they answered "let's talk about it" and glanced at the clock.

grounding: A colleague observes a worker who feels overlooked under a favouring manager making results visible, asking for criteria and considering moving on.
